sources.section: Build your own Front-end Framework / Library
sources.entry: JavaScript: _A DIY guide to build your own React_

summary.one_liner: Didact is a step-by-step tutorial repository that teaches how to build a simplified version of React from scratch, following a series of blog posts.
summary.what_it_does: The repository accompanies a blog post series that walks through building React step by step. The series covers rendering DOM elements, element creation and JSX, the virtual DOM and reconciliation, components and state, Fiber-based incremental reconciliation, and Hooks. Each post links to a CodePen or CodeSandbox code sample and, for most posts, to commit diffs showing the changes. The last post is described as self-contained and includes everything. A Chinese translation is linked for each post.
use_cases: follow a guided tutorial to write a React-like library
understand the virtual DOM and reconciliation
study how Fiber and Hooks are implemented
reference commit-by-commit code changes for a mini React
notable: Organized as a progressive blog post series, each step with a linked code sample
Per-post commit diffs show exactly what changed at each stage
Final post is self-contained and covers Fiber and Hooks
caveats: The README does not describe install or run steps; the code is used through the linked CodePen and CodeSandbox samples
Builds a teaching-scale React, not a production library
Some posts have no linked commits or code sample (e.g. Introduction)
